investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-08-12T12:32–12:39Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not place the requested kata peer-pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner collected zero evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing), causing every required-evidence assertion to fail.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity selector. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to schedule a new remote-agent pod times out (~142–152 s), preventing VM provisioning and leaving all required eval evidence unpopulated. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing peer-pods, leaving no capacity for new agent pods. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist.

TERTIARY — peer-pod provider quota or upstream VM quota exhaustion: the kata peer-pod provider (e.g., cloud VM quota) may have hit an external limit, causing the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource to report 0 allocatable on both eligible nodes.

QUATERNARY — cluster autoscaler not configured or unable to add kata-capable nodes: if autoscaling is enabled but no kata-capable node pool is available to scale out, new nodes would not carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and would not resolve the constraint.
